title: I built a bingo roguelike by talking to an AI that lives inside the game engine. Here is what that was actually like.
author: Fabulous-Eye7529
selftext:
**Written in partnership with Savi, the AI mentioned below.**

Hey, I’m Bran, or BranTheBroke. I’m a solo game designer with most of my experience in board games and TTRPGs, plus a little coding on the side.

For the past few months, I’ve been building games in Spawn, a browser-based engine with an AI collaborator named Savi built directly into it. It feels very different from asking a chatbot for code and pasting it into a project. Savi works inside the running game. I actually stumbled across the platform here and haven't looked back!

I can ask her to change how a charm works, then continue playing while she reads the game state, edits the code, and puts the change on my screen. There’s no exporting or restarting, and the game remains playable through the same link on desktop and mobile, even while I’m working on it.

The biggest surprise has been testing. We built three bot players: a rookie, an expert, and a “human” bot modeled on my own play history. They can run hundreds of games overnight and show me where the difficulty curve falls apart, which is the kind of testing I never expected to have as a solo developer.

It isn’t magic, though. Ambiguous instructions become design decisions I didn’t intend, changes sometimes arrive almost finished but miss something important, and hidden calculations can conceal bugs for weeks. Working this way is fast, but it still requires constant testing and a very clear idea of what the game should be.

The game is **Free Space**, a bingo roguelike inspired by *Balatro* where you rig both your card and the ball cage using charms, special squares, and increasingly strange rule combinations.

The demo is free and playable in a browser on mobile and desktop:

[https://www.spawn.co/@branthebroke/free-space](https://www.spawn.co/@branthebroke/free-space)

I designed every mechanic and made every balance decision, but I didn’t write any of the code. I still consider it a game I made, but with my co-creator, Savi, as well as the entire Spawn team.

Has anyone else tried building with an AI inside an engine rather than beside one?
